content.p:
Official cadastral surveying is governed by the Geoinformation Ordinance of 21 May 2008
SR 510.620 (GeoIO), unless there are special provisions in this present Ordinance.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

article.heading: Participation of the cantons and consultation of partner organisations

content.p: When preparing technical standards and other federal requirements that fall within the scope of this Ordinance but do not exclusively concern the Federal Administration, the Confederation shall ensure the participation of the cantons and the consultation of partner organisations in an appropriate manner.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 21 May 2008, in force since 1 July 2008 (AS 2008 2745).

content.p: The Federal Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport (DDPS) shall define the strategic plan for official cadastral surveying in consultation with the cantonal authorities responsible.
The cantons shall prepare implementation plans, which shall serve as the basis for the conclusion of programme agreements in accordance with Article 31 paragraph 2 GeoIA.

…
Repealed by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, with effect from 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).
Provisions concerning the surveying of military installations that derogate from those in this Ordinance are reserved.

Where military installations are transferred to civilian use, the DDPS shall regulate the procedure for their inclusion in the official cadastral survey and the allocation of costs.
Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

chapter.heading: Content of the Official Cadastral Survey

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

article.heading: Components of the official cadastral survey

blockList.listIntroduction: The components of the official cadastral survey are:

item.p: the data;
the fixed point and border point markers on the terrain (point markers);
the technical and administrative documents;
the components and principles of the cadastral survey under the previous system;

content.p: The DDPS shall regulate the details, in particular the products derived from the official cadastral survey data. Article 7 is reserved.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

article.heading: Geodata model for official cadastral surveying

content.p: The DDPS shall define the requirements for the geodata model for official cadastral surveying, in particular with regard to content, dimensions, accuracy and reliability. The geodata model may have a modular structure.
Cantonal extensions to the geodata model are not permitted.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 21 May 2008 (AS 2008 2745). Repealed by No 1 of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, with effect from 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).
Inserted by No I of the O of 7 March 2003 (AS 2003 507). Repealed by No I of the O of 21 May 2008, with effect from 1 July 2008 (AS 2008 2745).
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

content.p: The land register plan is an analogue or digital extract from the official cadastral survey data.

blockList.listIntroduction: It shall contain as a minimum the data on:

item.p: the border points and boundary lines of the land or buildings (Art. 943 para. 1 no 1 CC);
the border points and boundary lines of distinct and permanent rights to immovable property that have been defined in terms of area (Art. 943 para. 1 no 2 CC);
mines (Art. 943 para. 1 no. 3 CC);
areas subject to continuous movement (Art. 660a CC).

content.p: The minimum content of the plan has the effect of being recorded in the land register (Art. 971-974 CC).
The cantons may, in addition to the official cadastral survey data, require boundaries of easements to be indicated, provided their positions are clearly defined on the ground.

The Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP) and the DDPS shall jointly determine the requirements for the land register plan and other extracts, in particular with regard to content and presentation.

authorialNote.p: Repealed by No I of the O of 7 March 2003, with effect from 1 April 2003 (AS 2003 507).
Repealed by No I of the O of 23 March 2023, with effect from 1 April 2024 (AS 2023 529).

content.p: Marking involves establishing boundaries and placing boundary markers (monumentation).

Marking is required for territorial boundaries, property boundaries and boundaries of distinct and permanent rights over others’ land (easements), provided the latter can be clearly delimited by boundary lines. Article 17 is reserved.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).
The cantons shall enact regulations on the procedure for legally valid marking in accordance with this Ordinance.
In general, boundaries shall be established by inspecting the location.

blockList.listIntroduction: The cantons may specify that boundaries be established on the basis of plans, aerial photographs or other suitable means:

item.p:
in agricultural and forest land in mountainous and summer pasture areas as defined in the agricultural production register
Amended by No I of the O of 7 March 2003, in force since 1 April 2003 (AS 2003 507)., and in unproductive areas;

item.num:
b.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).
item.p: in the course of an updating process, subject to the agreement of the landowners concerned.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

content.p: A valid boundary line between two adjacent border points may be a straight line or an arc.
In the initial survey, or when finalising or updating the survey, a simple boundary line should be aimed for. Existing boundary lines should be improved where possible.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 21 May 2008 (AS 2008 2745). Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

content.p: Discrepancies between the cadastral survey data and the situation on the terrain or between the land register plan and other official cadastral survey plans shall be resolved ex officio, taking into account Article 668 paragraph 2 of the Swiss Civil Code.
Boundary markers shall be placed so that boundaries are permanently identifiable on the ground or can be found by simple means.

As a rule, the boundary markers must be placed before the boundaries are surveyed for the first time.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

blockList.listIntroduction: Individual boundary markers may be placed after the data is recorded in accordance with paragraph 1:

item.p: in the course of updating, unless the boundary was established by inspecting the location;
if there are compelling reasons why it was not possible or expedient to carry out the work earlier.

content.p: The boundary markers that are missing in accordance with paragraph 2 must be placed as soon as circumstances allow.
If boundaries are defined by natural or artificial limits that are permanent and clearly identifiable, monumentation is generally not required.

blockList.listIntroduction: The cantons may provide for further exceptions, in particular:

item.p: in areas where properties and distinct and permanent rights defined in area are made subject to consolidation;

item.num:
b.
Amended by No I of the O of 7 March 2003, in force since 1 April 2003 (AS 2003 507).
item.p: for properties and distinct and permanent rights defined in area whose boundary markers are continually threatened by agricultural activity or other encroachments;

item.num:
c.
Amended by No I of the O of 7 March 2003, in force since 1 April 2003 (AS 2003 507).
item.p: on agricultural and forest land in mountainous and summer pasture areas as defined in the agricultural production register, and in unproductive areas.

chapter.heading:
Initial Survey, Finalisation, Updating and Pilot Projects
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 764).

content.p: An initial survey is the production of the components of official cadastral surveying in areas that have not been previously subject to a fully approved cadastral survey and in areas defined in Article 51 paragraphs 3 and 4.

Finalisation is defined as the revision or expansion of a fully recognised official cadastral survey in order to adapt it to current regulations.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).
Updating is the modification of the components of official cadastral surveying to reflect changes in the legal or factual circumstances.

The Federal Directorate of Cadastral Surveying
Name in accordance with No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529). This amendment has been made throughout the document. may issue directives concerning methods for initial survey, finalisation and updating.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 21 May 2008, in force since 1 July 2008 (AS 2008 2745).

content.p:
The position and height references for official cadastral surveying are governed by Articles 4 and 5 GeoIO
SR 510.620.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 21 May 2008, in force since 1 July 2008 (AS 2008 2745).

content.p: The Federal Directorate of Cadastral Surveying and the competent cantonal authority shall plan official cadastral surveying on the basis of a programme agreement.
The canton shall determine when individual surveys are to be carried out. It shall regulate the consultation procedure.

…
Repealed by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, with effect from 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).
All components of the official cadastral survey are subject to updating.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

content.p: In cases where a reporting system for updating can be organised, the components of the official cadastral survey shall be updated within one year of a change occurring.
The cantons may, after consulting the Federal Directorate of Cadastral Surveying, provide for different time limits in justified cases.
They shall regulate the reporting system.
All data that is not subject to continuous updating shall be updated periodically.
Each periodic updating process must cover a large area forming a cohesive whole.

The periodic updating cycle should, if possible, correspond to that of the National Land Survey. It shall not exceed twelve years. The DDPS shall regulate the details of updating.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

authorialNote.p: Repealed by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, with effect from 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

content.p: All of the components of official cadastral surveying are subject to verification of quality and completeness by the cantonal oversight authority for surveying in accordance with the directives of the Federal Directorate of Cadastral Surveying;

authorialNote.p: Repealed by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, with effect from 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).
Amended by No I of the O of 21 May 2008, in force since 1 July 2008 (AS 2008 2745).

content.p:
After completion of an initial survey or the finalisation of an official cadastral survey and the elimination of discrepancies in accordance with Article 14a where the rights of landowners are affected, a public inspection procedure with objection procedures shall be arranged.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

The subject of the public inspection procedure is the land register plan for the area concerned and other extracts from the official cadastral survey data relating to the maintenance of the land register.

blockList.listIntroduction: The cantons shall regulate the procedure, subject to the following principles:

item.p: The public inspection procedure lasts for 30 days.
Official notice is given of the inspection procedure.

item.num:
c.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).
item.p: Property owners whose addresses are known shall in addition be informed by standard post of the public inspection procedure and of the legal remedies available to them.

d.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529). On request, the landowner shall be provided with an extract from the plan for the land register relating to his or her property in accordance with Article 7 paragraph 2 letters a-c.
An appeal against the objection decision may be filed with a cantonal authority; the authority shall review the decision without restriction.

A final appeal at cantonal level may be made to a court in accordance with Article 75 paragraph 2 of the Federal Supreme Court Act of 17 June 2005
SR 173.110.

content.p:
The cantons may stipulate that the public inspection procedure be conducted and official notice thereof be given exclusively by electronic means.
Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 7 March 2003, in force since 1 April 2003 (AS 2003 507).

content.p:
After completion of the public inspection procedure and after first instance objections have been dealt with, the competent cantonal authority shall approve the cadastral survey data, the extracts derived from them and, in particular, the land register plan, irrespective of any disputes yet to be resolved by court action, provided that the data meet the technical and quality requirements under federal law.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).
This approval confers the probative value of official public documents on the cadastral survey work.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Directorate of Cadastral Surveying shall recognise the cadastral survey if:

item.p: its formal examination has shown that the data meet the requirements of federal law; and
the surveying work has been approved by the canton.

content.p: It shall specify the documents to be submitted by the competent cantonal authority.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 7 March 2003 (AS 2003 507). Repealed by No I of the O of 21 May 2008, with effect from 1 July 2008 (AS 2008 2745).

Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023(AS 2022 764).
section.heading: Pilot projects

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Directorate of Cadastral Surveying may authorise pilot projects relating to official cadastral surveying in individual cantons or in specific geographical areas in order to test and develop:

item.p: new processes and competences;
new technologies;
new content, and geodata and cartographic specifications.

blockList.listIntroduction: The DDPS shall, with the agreement of the federal authorities concerned, issue in a separate ordinance for the pilot project concerned the provisions that derogate from:

item.p: this Ordinance;

the GeoIO
SR 510.620;

the Land Register Ordinance of 23 September 2011
SR 211.432.1;

the Ordinance of 21 May 2008
SR 510.625 on Geographical Names;

the FDJP and DDPS Technical Ordinance of 28 December 2012
SR 211.432.11 on the Land Register.

content.p: Pilot projects must be for a limited period and must be evaluated.

chapter.heading: Administration of Official Cadastral Surveying

article.heading:
…

content.p: The components of the official cadastral survey must be managed so as to guarantee their continued existence, integrity and quality at all times.

The DDPS shall regulate the technical and organisational requirements for administration, in particular data security, as well as archiving and historicisation in accordance with Articles 13-16 GeoIO
SR 510.620.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

chapter.heading: Data Access and Data Use

content.p: Any person may have access to the official cadastral survey data on demand, in accordance with the regulations in Articles 10–13 GeoIA.
The canton shall designate the agency which is to be responsible for deciding on access and use and for providing extracts and derived products.

The Federal Office of Topography shall operate a geoservice for networked access to cadastral surveying data (Art. 36 let. e GeoIO
SR 510.620).
Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

article.heading: Description provided for extracts and derived products

content.p: Extracts and derived products from official cadastral surveying should be provided together with the available metadata, including, as a minimum, information on the currency, quality and completeness of the data.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

content.p: Access to official cadastral survey data must be guaranteed by means of a download service.
The DDPS shall regulate the technical and organisational details of the service.
It may provide for other interfaces.

Certified extracts are extracts from the official cadastral survey data in analogue (hard copy) or digital form whose conformity with the definitive official cadastral survey data has been authenticated by a registered surveyor who is authorised to certify extracts under Article 46a paragraph 1 letter b.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).
Certified extracts are official public documents in accordance with Article 9 of the Swiss Civil Code.

…
Repealed by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, with effect from 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

authorialNote.p: Repealed by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, with effect from 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

content.p: Unless the exchange of data among authorities is regulated by an agreement under Article 14 paragraph 3 GeoIA, payment for the supply of official cadastral survey data to federal authorities shall be based solely on the time involved and the order-related costs.

The Federal Directorate of Cadastral Surveying (FDCA) is the specialist federal agency. The FDCS is headed by a registered surveyor.
Amended by No I of the O of 21 May 2008, in force since 1 July 2008 (AS 2008 2745).
The FDCS is responsible for the overall management and oversight of all aspects of official cadastral surveying.

The FDCS shall ensure the implementation and enforcement of regulations on the technical and quality requirements for official cadastral surveying.
Amended by No I of the O of 21 May 2008, in force since 1 July 2008 (AS 2008 2745).

The FCDS shall, in cooperation with the cantons, the Federal Office for Land Registry and Real Estate Law and the partner organisations, ensure the continual development of the geodata model for official cadastral surveying; it may set up working groups for this purpose.
Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

The FDCS shall also ensure coordination between official cadastral surveying and other federal surveying programmes, advise the federal authorities on the acquisition of official cadastral survey data, and represent the interests of the Confederation in dealings with the cantons and third parties.
Amended by No I of the O of 7 March 2003, in force since 1 April 2003 (AS 2003 507).

In cooperation with the cantonal surveying oversight authorities, the FDCS is entitled to process data on individual surveying projects and on the contractors responsible therefor.
Inserted by No I of the O of 7 March 2003 (AS 2003 507). Amended by Annex 2 No II 28 of the Data Protection Ordinance of 31 Aug. 2022, in force since 1 Sept. 2023 (AS 2022 568).

…
Repealed by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, with effect from 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

section.heading:
Survey Oversight
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

article.heading:
Cantonal Oversight Authority for Surveying
Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

content.p:
The canton shall appoint the agency (the Oversight Authority for Surveying) responsible for the oversight of official cadastral surveying. This agency shall be headed by a registered surveyor, who shall not be subject to directives on technical matters.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

The Oversight Authority for Surveying shall manage, monitor and verify the official cadastral surveying work. It shall ensure the coordination of the official cadastral surveying work with other surveying programmes and geoinformation systems.
Amended by No I of the O of 21 May 2008, in force since 1 July 2008 (AS 2008 2745).

If a canton is unable to fulfil its oversight role due to its actual circumstances, it may delegate its responsibilities in whole or in part to the Federal Directorate of Cadastral Surveying, subject to repayment of the costs involved.

The cantons may delegate survey oversight to each other or establish joint institutions for survey oversight.
Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 21 May 2008, in force since 1 July 2008 (AS 2008 2745).

article.heading: Administrative agreement with the Principality of Liechtenstein

content.p: The DDPS may conclude a rescindable fixed-term agreement under international law with the Principality of Liechtenstein covering the full or partial delegation of survey oversight for Liechtenstein to the Federal Directorate of Cadastral Surveying.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 21 May 2008, in force since 1 July 2008 (AS 2008 2745).

content.p: The canton is responsible for carrying out official cadastral surveying.
The canton shall appoint the agency which is to be responsible for the original and definitive data set of official cadastral surveying.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

article.heading: Right to carry out the work

content.p: The work of official cadastral surveying may only be carried out by registered surveyors not subject to directives, or under their technical supervision.

The DDPS may permit the conduct of official cadastral surveying work by other specialists provided the quality of their work satisfies the requirements for official cadastral surveying and the work does not relate to the minimum content of the land register plan in accordance with Article 7 paragraph 2 or territorial boundaries.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 21 May 2008, in force since 1 July 2008 (AS 2008 2745).

content.p: The award of contracts for work such as marking, initial survey, finalisation, periodic updating and provisional digitising must comply with the regulations on public procurement in force in the canton.
Official cadastral surveying work to be carried out in a specific geographical area must be the subject of a public invitation to tender.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

content.p: The FDJP and the DDPS shall jointly regulate the main aspects of electronic business transactions between the official cadastral surveying offices and the land register offices.
The cantons shall otherwise regulate the relations between official cadastral surveying and the land register.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

article.heading: Deeds of mutation und certified extracts

blockList.listIntroduction: The cantons shall determine which registered surveyors:

item.p: may sign deeds of mutation;
may issue certified extracts under Article 37.

content.p:
The electronic issue of certified extracts shall be governed by the Ordinance of 8 December 2017
SR 211.435.1 on the Issue of Electronic Public Documents and Electronic Certifications.

chapter.heading:
Programme Agreements, Federal Contributions and Other Costs
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 764).

Programme Agreements
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 764).

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 23 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 764).

blockList.listIntroduction: The subject matter of programme agreements between the Federal Office of Topography and cantons are in particular:

item.p: the services provided by the canton;
the contributions paid by the Confederation;
management controls;
the details of financial oversight.

content.p: A programme agreement shall have a duration of four years. Sub-goals may be agreed for a shorter duration.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 764).

content.p: The canton shall submit a report to the Federal Office of Topography each year on the use of the contributions.

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Office of Topography shall carry out random checks on:

item.p: the implementation of individual measures in accordance with the programme goals;
the use of the contributions paid.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 764).

blockList.listIntroduction: The Federal Office of Topography shall withhold payment, in whole or in part, of instalments of federal contributions during the programme if the canton:

item.p: does not comply with the reporting requirement (Art. 47a para. 1);
is at fault in failing significantly to perform its part of the programme.

content.p: If it becomes apparent after the programme that performance was inadequate, the Federal Office of Topography shall request the canton to remedy the situation; it shall specify an appropriate period for doing so.

If performance is still inadequate after this period, the Federal Office of Topography shall request repayment to cover the value of inadequate performance, together with interest of 5 per cent (Art. 28 para. 2 of the Subsidies Act of 5 October 1990
SR 616.1).

section.heading:

content.p: The rules on calculating the federal contribution to the funding for official cadastral surveying are set out in the Annex.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 764).

content.p: The only allowable costs are those incurred in accordance with the regulations and in the cost-effective execution of the task.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following costs are not allowable:

item.p: the costs of continuous updating and administration;

item.num:
b.
Repealed by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, with effect from 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

item.p: the costs of the cantonal oversight authority for surveying;
compensation paid to cantonal and communal bodies for their assistance in the work of marking and surveying;
the costs of cantonal verification and public inspection procedures;
compensation for crop damage during surveying work;
interest on advance payments for marking and surveying work;
additional costs resulting from non-observance by the contracting parties of the relevant regulations or of the terms of the contract;
the determination of building addresses;
the costs of correcting discrepancies in accordance with Article 14a.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 23 Nov. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 764).

content.p: For work that was awarded in accordance with the regulations on public procurement, the allowable costs shall correspond to the stipulated price, subject to Article 47d.
For work that was not awarded in accordance with the regulations on public procurement, the canton shall fix the allowable compensation in accordance with current market rates.
Compensation fixed by the canton requires the approval of the Confederation.
A flat-rate federal contribution may be agreed in the programme agreement instead of the allowable costs.

content.p: The cantons shall specify who is to be responsible for the remaining costs after deduction of the federal contribution.

content.p: Provisionally approved surveys must be modified by an initial survey (resurvey) in accordance with the new regulations.
Fully approved surveys must be finalised subject to the reservation of paragraph 3.

The DDPS shall regulate which fully approved surveys carried out under the regulations in force before 10 June 1919 must be replaced by initial survey (resurvey) in accordance with the new regulations.

In fully approved surveys based on fixed point networks that are not in the national coordinate system, the adjustment of the control network to satisfy the new regulations is deemed to be equivalent to an initial survey.
Amended by No I of the O of 7 March 2003, in force since 1 April 2003 (AS 2003 507).

Surveys approved in accordance with this Ordinance are considered to be valid surveys under the new regulations.
Inserted by No I of the O of 21 May 2008, in force since 1 July 2008 (AS 2008 2745).

article.heading: Initial surveys, finaliation, surveys in progress

content.p: The cantonal oversight authority for surveying shall determine whether initial surveys and finalisation that began less than two years after this Ordinance comes into force are to be conducted in accordance with the old or the new regulations.

The cantonal oversight authority for surveying shall decide, in consultation with the Federal Directorate of Cadastral Surveying, whether, and if necessary to what extent, surveys in progress at the time this Ordinance comes into force should be completed in accordance with the new regulations.

The cantonal oversight authority for surveying shall, in consultation with the Federal Directorate of Cadastral Surveying, decide whether, and if necessary to what extent, surveys carried out under the old regulations should be updated in accordance with the new regulations.

For work carried out or continued in accordance with the previous regulations as a result of a cantonal decision under Articles 52 or 53, the Instruction of 10 June 1919
[BS 2 592; AS 1980 106] on the marking and surveying of land parcels and the Ordinance of 12 May 1971
[AS 1971 704; 1991 370 Annex No 2] on Cadastral Surveying continue to apply.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 7 March 2003, in force since 1 April 2003 (AS 2003 507).

content.p: The cantons may decide that original general maps or reproductions thereof may continue to be drawn up until the cadastral surveying data required for their replacement becomes available.
Existing general maps must continue to be updated in areas for which the cadastral surveying data necessary for their replacement is not yet available.

…
Repealed by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, with effect from 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

article.heading: Special measures for the preservation of land parcel surveys

content.p:
Provisional digitisation is considered to be covered under special measures for the preservation of land parcel surveys in accordance with Article 5 paragraph 3 of the Federal Decree of 20 March 1992
[AS 1992 2461; 1994 1612. AS 2007 5819 Art. 6]. See now: Federal Assembly O of 6 Oct. 2006 on the Funding of Official Cadastral Surveying (SR 211.432.27). on Compensation for Official Cadastral Surveying.
Amended by No I of the O of 7 March 2003, in force since 1 April 2003 (AS 2003 507).

Provisional digitisation is defined as the conversion of a provisionally or fully approved cadastral surveys under the old regulations into a digital form that does not or does not fully satisfy the requirements of the new cadastral surveying regulations.
Provisionally digitised surveys are deemed to be surveys under the old regulations.
The DDPS shall specify the requirements for provisional digitisation.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 21 May 2008, in force since 1 July 2008 (AS 2008 2745).

article.heading: Transitional Provisions to the Amendment of 21 May 2008

content.p: Until the agreement in accordance with Article 14 paragraph 3 GeoIA comes into force, data supplied to the federal authorities from official cadastral surveying shall be charged for only in accordance with actual time and associated costs.

…
Repealed by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, with effect from 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Aug. 2023, in force since 1 Jan. 2024 (AS 2023 529).

article.heading: Transitional Provisions to the Amendment of 23 August 2023

content.p: If the DDPS amends the requirements for the geodata model (Art. 6), it shall regulate the transition from the current to the amended geodata model.
In doing so, it shall specify which current provisions of this Ordinance on the geodata model continue to apply for a limited period.

blockList.listIntroduction: The information level for pipelines shall be abrogated in the following stages:

item.p:
The official geodata set for pipelines (Identifier 222) created with the Pipeline Safety Ordinance of 4 June 2021
SR 746.12 and the information level for pipelines in official cadastral surveying shall provisionally be managed and updated in parallel.
The Swiss Federal Office of Energy (SFOE) shall verify the data in the official geodata set for pipelines by using the data from the information level for pipelines.

The Federal Office of Topography shall in consultation with the SFOE determine the date on which the information level for pipelines for official cadastral surveying can be abrogated and deleted; it shall notify the cantons of this date and publish the decision in the Official Federal Gazette.

content.p: This Ordinance comes into force on 1 January 1993.

content.p: When calculating the federal contribution to the funding for cantonal projects in accordance with Article 47c, the following percentages apply; they determine the share of allowable costs in accordance with Articles 47d and 48:

item.p: for built-up areas and building zones (Zone I): 15 per cent;
for agricultural and forest land in valleys according to the agricultural production register (Zone II): 30 per cent;
for agricultural and forest land in mountainous and summer pasture areas according to the agricultural production register (Zone III): 45 per cent.

content.p: If a survey that was carried out in accordance with the regulations that applied before 10 June 1919 is replaced, the values in Number 1 apply.

item.p: for built-up areas and building zones (Zone I): 15 per cent;
for agricultural and forest land in valleys according to the agricultural production register (Zone II): 20 per cent;
for agricultural and forest land in mountainous and summer pasture areas according to the agricultural production register (Zone III): 35 per cent;

in the case of overall improvements and land reallotments in agriculture and forestry, provided the Confederation does not make payments for the same purpose under other legislation and provided these costs are not borne by third parties: 25 per cent.

content.p: Marking of territorial and property boundaries for agricultural and forest land in mountainous and summer pasture areas according to the agricultural production register (Zone III), provided the canton bears an appropriate share of the costs: 25 per cent.
For measures carried out following natural events or permanent landslip incidents and which are equivalent to an initial survey, the rates for an initial survey and marking apply.

item.p: for special adjustments of exceptional national interest, provided the canton demonstrates that the funding is guaranteed: 60 per cent;

for the costs of periodical updates that are not borne by the person responsible and the funding of which according to information from the canton is guaranteed, for each period in accordance with Article 24 paragraph 3: 60 per cent.

content.p: Innovative pilot projects to develop official cadastral surveying and to test new technologies: 50–90 per cent, depending on the innovative content and the federal interest.
